newsitem.title: UK: EIU sees world sugar output unchanged in 1996/97.
newsitem.headline: EIU sees world sugar output unchanged in 1996/97.

text.p: World sugar production should remain unchanged at 123.3 million tonnes in 1996/97 but rising consumption should cut the global surplus by half to 2.4 million, the Economist Intelligence Unit (EIU) said on Tuesday.

The EIU pegged 1996/97 sugar consumption at 120.9 million tonnes after 118.5 million in 1995/96. Figures refer to the September/August crop year. In its quarterly world commodity forecast, the EIU said sugar stocks would be much higher than previously expected in the remainder of 1995/96, mainly due to India's massive crop. "This has considerably raised the ratio of stocks to consumption but is not expected to have any marked effect on world prices for the time being," the report said.
Closing stocks were estimated at 43.9 million tonnes for 1996/97 after 41.5 million the previous season, while the stocks to consumption ratio was forecast at 36.3 percent after 35.0.
The EIU said it expected world market prices to start next calendar year at 11.00 cents/lb, based on the ISA daily average, and fall to 10.20 cents/lb by the fourth quarter.
